messages:
sara: Heads-up: seeing odd KV growth when longctx sessions hit ~1200 tokens. Allocation keeps creeping despite evictions.

kai: I saw that on the dedicated canary too. Fragmentation pattern — lots of tiny slab allocations after repeated prefix churn. Heap growth ~30MB/hr on the canary box.

miguel: Can you share a repro trace or sample logs? Which workloads show this most clearly?

sara: Repro: multi-turn assistant load. Many sessions share the same system prompt + first user message, then diverge. Prefix overlap ~35-45% across requests. Current cache key is `model:tenant:prefix_hash:session_id` which I think is the problem.

ana: +1 to looking at key shape. If session_id is baked into the lookup key we essentially prevent cross-session reuse even when prefixes are identical, so we fragment the address space.

perf-bot: perf/kvcache/miss_rate: canary_before=0.22 canary_after=0.39; p95_infer_lat += 6ms. (auto-report)

kai: Proposal: decouple lookup identity from stickiness. New lookup key = `model:tenant:prefix_fp:v2` (no session id). Session affinity is a separate hint header `X-RI-Session-Hint` used to soft-pin entries, not change lookup.

sara: Example pseudo: 
```
lookup_key = f"{model}:{tenant}:{prefix_fp_v2}"
entry = kv.lookup(lookup_key)
if entry and session_hint:
  entry.soft_pin(session_hint)
else:
  // normal access
```
Soft_pin metadata should not affect key equality.

miguel: For eviction, soft_pin reduces eviction_score but with TTL (e.g., 30s). It should be cheap to store (few bytes) and not prevent compaction. Also add a background compaction that coalesces tiny objects every 5m.

ana: Telemetry we need: per-prefix residency histogram, soft_pin hit rate, reused_across_sessions_count, and an eviction_score distribution. Add an experimental metric `prefix_crossreuse_enabled` per host to slice results.

kai: Canary plan: roll behind config flag `prefix_crossreuse=true`. Start at 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Gate on mem_growth_rate (< +10MB/hr), kv_miss_rate (no regression), and p95 latency (no >+10ms). If any trigger fires, flip flag off.

sara: Tenant isolation concern: keep tenant in the key. Also compute prefix_fp with tenant_salt to avoid cross-tenant collision risk. We should also version fp (v2) so we can revert easily.

miguel: Also ensure fingerprint normalization: strip ephemeral span ids, normalize whitespace and tokenization differences across model variants so same logical prefix maps to same fp even if tokenized differently between quantized variants.

ana: I'll own the telemetry and A/B harness PR. Will add dashboards for: mem gradient, per-prefix reuse ratio, soft_pin retention, reused_across_sessions, small-object-frag-ratio.

perf-bot: Note: schedule perf replay for 50k prefixes from canary bucket to estimate reuse delta (job queued).

sara: I will draft the runtime patch to compute prefix_fp_v2 and add soft_pin metadata and the compaction job. Will add config + rollout docs.

kai: Quick question: any concerns about attack surface (malicious prefixes causing hotset pinning)? We should limit soft_pin weight per-session or per-tenant.

miguel: Rate-limit soft_pin per session (max 10 pins/sec per session) and global per-tenant throttle. Also consider a decay multiplier so repeated pins diminish effect.

ana: Sounds good. I'll include those limits in the telemetry PR. Starting canary tomorrow morning.

sara: Thanks team. I'll open the runtime PR and link the canary checklist. :thumbsup:
